title: KV cache + batching + quantization: POC experiment log
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a focused POC series to evaluate interaction effects between KV-cache (prefix reuse), continuous batching, and various quantization strategies for latency-first customer workloads. Target environment: Dedicated small-pool (1-2 A10G-equivalent GPUs), interactive Q&A product with common short prompts (avg 35 tokens input, 75 tokens output). Goal: reach p50 < 60ms per token and p95 < 200ms while minimizing GPU memory and per-token cost.

Background and constraints:
- Customer constraints: single-region dedicated pool, strict data residency, cannot offload KV caching to external redis (must be in-GPU or ephemeral local).
- Workload: 70% prefix reuse (system prompts + few-shot examples), 30% cold-start queries. Burstiness: peaks ~450 rps for short bursts (15–30s).
- Models evaluated: rw-1.3B (fp16 baseline), rw-1.3B-8bit, rw-3B-4bit-awq (experimental), gpt-medium-6B (fp16), oc-2.7B-quant8

Experiment matrix (condensed):
1) Baseline (no KV cache, batch size 1, fp16 models)
2) KV-cache only (store prefix + KV in-GPU, batch size 1)
3) Batching only (continuous batching enabled, target batch 8, no KV)
4) KV + Batching (continuous batching + in-GPU KV cache)
5) KV + Batching + Quant (repeat 4 across quant variants: 8-bit GPTQ-style, 4-bit AWQ)

Key config knobs we toggled:
- continuous_batching.window_ms: 8 / 16 / 32
- continuous_batching.max_batch: 4 / 8 / 16
- kv_cache.mode: gpu_local / disabled
- quant.method: fp16 / int8-gptq / int4-awq
- kv_cache.evict_policy: lru / pinned-prefix-only
- routing.fallback: warm-only / allow-cold-fallback

Representative results (median of 10 min windows, steady state):
- Baseline fp16 (rw-1.3B): p50 token latency ~95ms, p95 ~320ms, throughput ~180 tps (tokens/sec), GPU mem 11.3GB
- KV-only fp16: p50 ~48ms (51% improvement), p95 ~205ms, throughput ~320 tps, GPU mem +0.8GB
- Batching only fp16 (max_batch=8, window_ms=16): p50 ~65ms, p95 ~240ms, throughput ~610 tps, GPU mem +0.5GB
- KV + Batching fp16: p50 ~36ms, p95 ~160ms, throughput ~780 tps, GPU mem +1.4GB
- KV + Batching + int8-gptq (rw-1.3B-8bit): p50 ~30ms, p95 ~145ms, throughput ~980 tps, GPU mem 6.2GB (reduced), slight quality delta on numeric fidelity tests (BLEU-like drop ~0.8 pts)
- KV + Batching + int4-awq (rw-3B-4bit-awq): p50 ~42ms, p95 ~170ms, throughput ~720 tps, GPU mem 4.1GB, quality regression noticeable on long-context hallucination cases (qualitative notes below)

Observations and tradeoffs:
- KV cache gives the single largest latency win for our prefix-heavy workload. Even with small batch sizes, caching the system prompt + examples reduces per-token generation calls.
- Continuous batching dramatically increases throughput but can hurt tail latency if window_ms is too large. 16ms with max_batch=8 hit a good sweet spot for 35/75 token requests in our environment.
- Quantization (8-bit GPTQ-style) delivered strong cost/memory benefits with minimal quality loss on short-answer tests. 4-bit AWQ gave extreme memory savings but increased long-context failure modes (more repetition/hallucination).
- Combined approach (KV+batching+8bit) provides multiplicative benefits: lower p50 and high throughput while keeping p95 within customer SLO.
- GPU memory: quantization allowed fitting more concurrent KV entries if we trade model precision. For instance, int8 allowed 2.5x more cached prefixes in the same GPU memory budget compared to fp16.

Quality notes (small eval set of 250 queries):
- int8-gptq vs fp16: exact-match drop ~1.2% on short-fact questions, semantics preserved in ~98% of samples. Noted differences when outputs required precise code formatting (tabs/spaces), investigate tokenizer rounding edge cases.
- int4-awq: acceptable for very short responses, but we observed a ~6% drop in coherence for responses >120 tokens and ~3% higher repetition score.

Stability and correctness issues encountered:
- KV eviction race: when pinned-prefix-only set, eviction logic mis-indexed after dynamic memory pressure spikes (investigated with SRE, root cause: stale pointer in cache metadata on cuda-memmove path). Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/432 (linked above).
- Batching fairness: long-running streaming requests were grouped and increased latency for short burst work. Mitigation: introduce token-budget-aware batching where streaming sessions are deprioritized for batch aggregation.

Cost approximation (per 1M tokens, rough):
- fp16 baseline: $7.2
- fp16 + KV + batching: $3.8
- int8 + KV + batching: $2.1
- int4 + KV + batching: $1.6 (but with quality caveats)
(These numbers include GPU amortized time + infra overhead, ballpark estimates for proposals.)

Actionable recommendations for POC deliverable:
1) Default config for customer trial: rw-1.3B-8bit (gptq style) + kv_cache=gpu_local (pinned-prefix-only) + continuous_batching.window_ms=16 + max_batch=8. Rationale: best balance of latency, throughput, memory.
2) Add regression suite: 1k prompt set covering code formatting, numeracy, and long-context recall to catch quantization regressions before rollout.
3) Implement token-budget-aware batching in runtime (short-term flag) to avoid long-stream drag on short queries.
4) Hardening: backfill fix for KV eviction race and add GPU memory watchdog and client backpressure signals.
5) Customer-facing notes: explain quant tradeoffs and offer an opt-in to either fp16 for max fidelity or int8 for cost/scale. Provide evaluation artifacts with the trial.

Next experiments (planned):
- Hybrid routing: route cold-start queries to fp16 gpt-medium-6B and warm (cached) queries to int8 smaller model to reduce cold-tail errors. Measure correctness drift.
- Dynamic quant profiles per-layer (mix-int8+fp16 on high-attention layers) to try to recover AWQ failures on long contexts.
- Evaluate multi-prefix coalescing to reduce KV duplication across similar few-shot examples.

Appendix: short snippets used during runs:
- Example continuous batching config: {window_ms: 16, max_batch: 8, max_latency_ms: 200} (we used JSON in runtime config UI)
- Example perf-check command: ./bench --model rw-1.3B-8bit --burst 400 --mix warm:0.7,cold:0.3 --avg_input 35 --avg_output 75 --duration 600

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need micro-bench for tokenizer boundary sensitivities under int8 to track formatting diffs.
- Check if pinning large prefixes causes disproportionate eviction on multi-tenant pools. Consider prefix dedup on ingest.
- Confirm licensing / redistribution constraints for the experimental AWQ variants before recommending to customers.

Summary: For prefix-heavy interactive POCs the fastest path to meet latency SLOs and cost targets is to combine an in-GPU KV cache with modest continuous batching and int8 quantization. 4-bit approaches are promising for strict memory-limited edge but require more QA for long-context integrity.

Recorded by: Asha Patel (SE)
Reviewers: Ethan Liu (Infra), Marina Kovács (Applied ML)
